subject: Creativity
title: Nikola Tesla: The Forgotten Visionary
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Nikola Tesla: The Forgotten Visionary.

hook.text: Tesla envisioned AC power, radio, and wireless energy. Edison got the fame. Tesla died alone in a hotel room.

buildup.text: He could visualize entire machines in his head, rotate them mentally, and identify flaws before building anything.

discovery.text: His AC motor design came in a flash during a walk in Budapest — he drew the circuit in the dirt with a stick.

twist.text: He held over 300 patents. But he gave away his most valuable one — AC royalties — to save Westinghouse from bankruptcy.

climax.text: Nearly everything in your home runs on Tesla's AC system. Edison's DC lost. History forgot who won.

punchline.text: Tesla powered the modern world. The world forgot to pay him.

quiz.question: How many patents did Nikola Tesla hold?

details.summary: Nikola Tesla envisioned alternating current, wireless communication, and wireless energy transmission decades before they became possible. His ability to visualize complete inventions in his mind before building them was extraordinary, but his inability to commercialize ideas left him forgotten...
details.whyItMatters: Tesla illustrates the gap between creative vision and commercial success. His story raises important questions about how societies reward and support creative genius versus business acumen.
takeaways: Tesla visualized complete working inventions mentally before building prototypes
His alternating current system powers civilization today
Brilliant creative vision without business skill led to poverty and obscurity

faq.question: How did Tesla visualize inventions?
faq.answer: Tesla described an extraordinary ability to construct complete three-dimensional machines in his mind, run them mentally, and identify flaws before building physical prototypes. He attributed this to childhood visualization exercises that became an involuntary mental process.

faq.question: Why was Tesla forgotten for so long?
faq.answer: Edison's superior business skills and promotional ability overshadowed Tesla's contributions. Tesla died in poverty in 1943, and his role in developing the electrical infrastructure of modern civilization was largely uncredited until a revival of interest began in the 2000s.
